programmes.d: Micah is terrorized by an old enemy and resigns from his job.
A visit to Micah's old home leads to the uncovering of an old mystery.
Blinded in an explosion, Lucas fights despair as he prepares for a meeting with a gun-toting enemy.
A deranged ex-prisoner of war captures Lucas, locks him in a cage and vows to make him suffer.
A traveling salesman can't talk his way out of an assault charge.
Lucas is threatened with hanging when some horses he has purchased town turn out to be stolen.
A janitor-turned-gunfighter's reputation hangs on one lucky shot and a lot of gall.
Lucas tries to get help when he is shot after witnessing a murder.
After being foreman of a jury that convicted an Apache, Lucas is marked for death.
Lucas allows some snowed-in stagecoach passengers to stay with him until the roads are passable.
Two pranksters write away for a mail-order bride, using Lucas's name.
Lucas recognizes Dr. Battle as an ex-gunslinger with whom he once fought.
A Chinese man and his son fight prejudice as they try to open a laundry in North Fork.
Lucas and Mark are traveling across the Mexican desert amd encounter a trio of Mexican bandits.
Mark takes a job as a stable boy against his father's wishes.
Mark and Milly are held hostage in her general store when two gunmen attempt a daring robbery.
Two prison wagon drivers stop at the McCain ranch looking for whiskey.
Mark goes to work for Will Temple, a badly scarred, very mysterious rancher.
Corey Hazlett insists he's innocent of murder, despite Lucas's eyewitness testimony.
Lucas tries to dissuade a latter-day knight from rushing into battle.
Abe Lincoln's claim that he's the Great Emancipator amuses everyone except Matt Yordy.
The North Fork Town Council feels that an old man is incapable of raising his grandson.
Mark Twain visits North Fork and quickly alienates the townspeople.
Lucas tries to stop embittered John Holliver from venting his wrath.
Lucas is accidentally responsible for the death of a young mountain boy.
Lucas is stunned when Mark is kidnapped and a $5,000 ransom is asked.
Lucas seeks an escape when he's captured by outlaws while seeking help for an injured Mark.
The young Queen-to-be of France hides out in North Fork with her sick brother.
A notorious killer is being held in the North Fork jail and word gets out.
Lucas's old Army pal settles in North Fork with his deaf daughter.
An Englishman arrives with a custom-made rifle and a plan to kill Lucas.
Mark falls head-over-heels in puppy love.
A young man arrives in North Fork to claim the body of his dead brother.
The son of a man allegedly murdered in North Fork comes to town to kill Micah.
Lucas is accused of murder by a man who claims to be an eyewitness.
Lucas and Mark stop on the way to the county fair to deliver a message to Micah.
Mark and Milly are shocked when Lucas begins gambling.
Mark befriends Lafayette Bly, a blind man with an acute sense of hearing and a very strong grip.
The McCains get new neighbors when a couple moves into a nearby ranch.
A Southern belle arrives in North Fork claiming that Micah is her husband.
Lucas is torn by conflicting emotions when he meets the town's new preacher, a former outlaw.
Marshall and outlaw are friends.
A gambler moves into North Fork and begins courting a local girl.
Lucas develops temporary amnesia from a head injury while visiting a strange town.
A former neighbor of the McCains' is released from jail after serving his sentence for robbery.
When Lucas, Mark, and Micah get lost in Old Mexico, they are held hostage by a group of bandits.
